sources.title: Brazil Country Climate and Development Report: Executive Summary
sources.temporal_coverage: Current climate-risk diagnostic, historical loss estimates and modeled poverty impacts through 2030.
sources.methodology: Executive summary distills modeled national climate risks, poverty pathways and sector and institutional options.
sources.limitations: Only the 14-page executive summary was used; projections do not establish local incidence.

sources.title: Severe droughts reduce river navigability and isolate communities in the Brazilian Amazon
sources.organization: Communications Earth & Environment; authors from Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais and partner research institutions
sources.temporal_coverage: Settlement datasets dated 2020-2021; reported drought impacts from 2000-2020; hydrological series assessed through 2021.
sources.methodology: Maps settlement proximity to rivers and roads, codes reported drought impacts and analyzes 90 river-gauge time series.
sources.limitations: Media-reported impacts are incomplete; distance screening indicates isolation risk, not observed isolation for each settlement.

sources.title: Climate-related Crisis in the Amazon Region: Flash Update No. 1, Reporting Period August-September 2024
sources.organization: UNICEF Latin America and Caribbean Regional Office
sources.temporal_coverage: Situation and response snapshot for August-September 2024, with near-term risks and planned UNICEF actions.
sources.methodology: Flash update combines state, Indigenous-organization and humanitarian coordination data with UNICEF response monitoring.
sources.limitations: Dated situation snapshot; some population and service figures are relayed from third parties, not a prevalence study.

sources.title: Impact of drought in the Brazilian Amazon and 2025 outlook
sources.temporal_coverage: Secondary review of the 2023-2024 drought and humanitarian access conditions, with outlook for 2025.
sources.methodology: Seven-page thematic report based on review of public secondary sources.
sources.limitations: Remote-area needs and access data are explicitly scarce; armed-group information is synthesized from cited sources.

sources.title: Impacts of the Floods in Rio Grande do Sul: Observations and Recommendations for the Guarantee of Economic, Social, Cultural, and Environmental Rights
sources.organization: Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, Special Rapporteurship on Economic, Social, Cultural and Environmental Rights (REDESCA)
sources.temporal_coverage: Mission conducted December 2-6, 2024, documenting impacts and response to the April-May 2024 floods.
sources.methodology: December 2024 mission, meetings with authorities, civil society, scientists and affected communities, plus document review.
sources.limitations: State-specific mission; reported figures draw partly on administrative and secondary sources, not a representative survey.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 3-4, climate impacts and poverty pathways
claims.paraphrase: The World Bank reports reduced water availability and longer droughts; urban-poor residents, especially in informal settlements, are particularly vulnerable to extreme-weather losses.
claims.limitations: National diagnostic; it does not provide city-level incidence.

claims.locator: One-based PDF p. 4, modeled extreme-poverty pathway
claims.paraphrase: Climate shocks could place 800,000-3 million more people in extreme poverty by 2030, depending on Brazil's development pathway.
claims.scenario: The executive summary gives a range across development pathways but does not specify an SSP or RCP scenario.
affected_groups: people at risk of extreme poverty
claims.limitations: Modeled range, not an observed poverty effect.

claims.locator: One-based PDF p. 7, adaptive social protection
claims.paraphrase: The World Bank says Brazil's adaptive social protection system has scalability and timeliness constraints; it recommends climate-risk data in the social registry.
affected_groups: families and communities exposed to climate shocks
claims.limitations: 2023 diagnostic and recommendations, not an implementation evaluation.

claims.locator: One-based PDF p. 2, Fig. 1 and settlement-isolation screening
claims.paraphrase: A drought-isolation screen identified 1,850 non-Indigenous localities, 1,495 in Amazonas; 755 of 1,359 screened Indigenous villages were also there.
claims.limitations: Proximity to waterways and roads is a risk screen, not observed isolation for each settlement.

claims.locator: One-based PDF p. 4, hydrological analysis and Fig. 4
claims.paraphrase: Across 90 river gauges, 2005, 2010 and 2016 had low-water periods about 36.8 days above the 2000-2021 median.
claims.limitations: Historical gauge comparison; it is not an attribution estimate.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 1-2 and 6, abstract, Fig. 6 and impacts discussion
claims.paraphrase: Low rivers disrupt navigation and isolate rural communities, restricting access to food, fuel, medicine, health care and education.
claims.limitations: Impacts are coded from media accounts and are not comprehensive service records.

claims.locator: One-based PDF p. 7, drought-related environmental governance and services
claims.paraphrase: One media account reported that low-water navigation constraints hindered environmental enforcement against deforestation, hunting and illegal logging.
claims.limitations: Single media account within a broader impact review; no national effect estimate.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 1-2, highlights and Brazil needs assessment
claims.paraphrase: An Amazonas update counted 745,000 drought-affected people; 330,000, including 115,000 children, lived in 2,200 Indigenous and riverside communities isolated or at risk.
claims.limitations: Snapshot figure uses the Amazonas state update; it is not a current post-2024 count.

claims.locator: One-based PDF p. 2, Brazil needs assessment and response actions
claims.paraphrase: The update relays that Amazonas declared emergencies in 62 municipalities and distributed food, water purifiers, tanks and medical supplies.
claims.limitations: Actions are reported at the September 2024 snapshot; effectiveness was not evaluated.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 1 and 3, highlights and expected evolution
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF flags family separation, violence and exploitation risks for children amid drought and fires; prolonged crisis could prompt family movement and add protection risks.
claims.scenario: Conditional on the crisis persisting; the flash update does not quantify likelihood or resulting incidents.
claims.limitations: Risk statements, not reported incidence estimates.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNICEF links drought and wildfire disruption or movement to child-protection violence and exploitation risks.

claims.locator: One-based PDF p. 1, crisis overview and access conditions
claims.paraphrase: ACAPS says armed groups exploiting resources, recruiting communities or forcing displacement aggravate drought-affected access, especially in Amazonas.
claims.limitations: Secondary review; its cited armed-group evidence was not independently rechecked here.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: ACAPS explicitly says insecurity combined with drought has hampered access in northwest Brazil.

claims.locator: One-based PDF p. 1, access risks and affected groups
claims.paraphrase: ACAPS says river isolation heightens exposure to trafficking, forced labour and abuse; women bear added burdens when drought reduces crops or livestock.
claims.limitations: The report gives a secondary synthesis, not incident-level prevalence estimates.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: ACAPS explicitly connects drought-related river isolation with heightened exploitation risks.

claims.paraphrase: In Rio Grande do Sul, 88% of quilombola communities were flood-affected; 84 Indigenous communities and about 16,691 people also faced disrupted services and subsistence.
claims.limitations: Administrative and mission-reported figures use different group denominators.

claims.paraphrase: The Commission reports incomplete river monitoring and Porto Alegre flood-defense failures, with maintenance and design weaknesses limiting warnings, evacuation and protection.
institutions: Civil Defense of Rio Grande do Sul
claims.limitations: The report summarizes expert and mission evidence; it is not an engineering audit.

claims.paraphrase: The Commission received reports of gender-based violence in shelters in Porto Alegre and other municipalities and recommended specific protection protocols for climate emergencies.
claims.limitations: Reports indicate cases, not prevalence across shelters or affected populations.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report records gender-based violence reports in shelters during the climate-disaster response.

search_audit.query: Brazil subnational climate vulnerability drought flood Amazon Cerrado Rio Grande do Sul Indigenous quilombola official report
search_audit.outcome: Read the World Bank executive summary, Amazon drought study and UNICEF situation update; read the IACHR flood mission report for state- and group-specific impacts.

search_audit.query: Brazil climate drought armed groups violence Indigenous Amazon conflict exploitation climate change report
search_audit.outcome: UNICEF flags child-protection violence/exploitation risks in drought and wildfire disruption; ACAPS states armed-group insecurity aggravates drought access. Neither establishes climate-caused armed conflict.

search_audit.query: Brazil armed insecurity obstructs climate adaptation drought response access river communities reverse FCV pathway
search_audit.outcome: ACAPS says insecurity with drought hampered access in northwest Brazil; the Amazon study reports a single account of low navigation hindering environmental enforcement. No inspected source establishes armed conflict blocking formal adaptation delivery.

search_audit.query: Brazil climate resilience capacity adaptive social protection drought response Amazonas water services Rio Grande do Sul flood preparedness
search_audit.outcome: Reviewed World Bank adaptive-social-protection diagnostics, state drought relief reported by UNICEF and IACHR findings on flood monitoring, defenses and emergency violence-prevention needs.

gaps: No inspected source establishes climate-caused armed or intercommunal conflict in Brazil. The source-stated pathways here concern drought/insecurity-related humanitarian access and violence/exploitation risks for children, and gender-based violence reported in flood shelters; these are not synthesized into an armed-conflict causal chain.
The Amazon hydrology paper analyzes 2000-2021 gauge data and media-coded impacts; UNICEF's update is a September 2024 snapshot, and ACAPS explicitly reports sparse remote-area assessment data.
The REDESCA report concerns Rio Grande do Sul's 2024 flood response; its findings are not generalized to other states.
A 2025 article specifically addressing climate change, Indigenous Amazon peoples and violence was located, but its publisher page returned 403; no claim was taken from its search metadata.
